title: I Posted the Fencing-Piste Clock After the Coach Camped Our Numbered Strip

parts.text: I stepped into strip three at 6:05 p.m. and coach Ivo was already using our numbered reels. The board said: ONE STRIP. SIXTY MINUTES. REELS STAY WITH THE BOOKING. I was twenty-six, club secretary, holding a clipboard that listed our bout. Ivo shrugged. "Coaches are the piste." I photographed the board, the booking, and his lunge on our strip. Then I asked for the piste clock. At 6:13 the armory desk pinged why Ivo's name was on strip three. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The armory desk can see Ivo's lunge on strip three during our bout.

social.video_title: He camped our numbered fencing strip — Part 1/2
social.description: Fencing salle, a coach on our strip, a sixty-minute clock he posted. I logged the lunge. Would you have asked for the piste clock?

parts.text: Ivo called it footwork until the desk asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the strip still. The reels went back to our numbered hooks. Ivo ran a slot of their own and told the next coach atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: COACHES ARE NOT THE PISTE. I keep our bout on a labeled card. Ivo brown-bags his lunges. The strip finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Coaches are not the piste — Part 2/2
social.description: Piste clock, numbered reels, and a second line on the board. Was footwork ever our bout?
